title.zh: 卷26 列傳第18 長孫儉 長孫紹遠 弟澄 兄子兕 斛斯徵
title.en: Volume 26 Biographies 18: Zhang Sunjian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; younger brother Cheng; elder brother Si; Hu Sizheng
title.raw: 卷26 列傳第18 長孫儉 長孫紹遠 弟澄 兄子兕 斛斯徵 Volume 26 Biographies 18: Zhang Sunjian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; younger brother Cheng; elder brother Si; Hu Sizheng

sentences.zh: 長孫儉 長孫紹遠 弟澄 兄子兕 斛斯徵

translations.literal: Zhangsun Jian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; younger brother Cheng; elder brother's son Si; Hu Sizheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; Zhangsun Cheng (younger brother); Zhangsun Si (nephew); Hu Sizheng

sentences.zh: 長孫儉，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Jian was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 本名慶明。

translations.literal: His original name was Qingming.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Qingming.

sentences.zh: 其先，魏之枝族，姓托拔氏。

translations.literal: His forebears were a branch clan of Wei, surnamed Tuoba.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were a cadet line of Wei bearing the surname Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 孝文遷洛，改為長孫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, [the surname] was changed to Zhangsun.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the family took the surname Zhangsun.

sentences.zh: 五世祖嵩，魏太尉、北平王。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Song was Wei Grand Commandant and Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Song had been Grand Commandant of Wei and Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 儉少方正，有操行，狀貌魁梧，神彩嚴肅，雖在私室，終日儼然。

translations.literal: Jian from youth was upright and proper, had moral conduct; his stature was imposing, his expression dignified and stern; even in private chambers, all day he remained solemnly composed.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Zhangsun Jian was upright and principled, with a imposing frame and a grave, commanding presence; even in private he sat all day with unbroken dignity.

sentences.zh: 性不妄交，非其同志，雖貴遊造門，亦不與相見。

translations.literal: By nature he did not associate casually; those not of like mind, even if noble travelers came to his door, he would not meet with them.
translations.idiomatic: He made no casual friendships; if a man was not of his mind, no matter how highborn the visitor at his gate, he would not receive him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，起家員外散騎侍郎，從爾朱天光破隴右。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang, he first entered office as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and followed Erzhu Tianguang to defeat Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he entered service as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and followed Erzhu Tianguang in the conquest of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨夏州，以儉為錄事，深器敬之。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived at Xia Province, he made Jian recorder-in-chief and held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took up post at Xia Province, he appointed Zhangsun Jian recorder-in-chief and valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳被害，太祖赴平涼，凡有經綸謀策，儉皆參預。

translations.literal: When He Ba Yue was murdered, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went to Pingliang; for every grand strategy and plan, Jian participated.
translations.idiomatic: After He Ba Yue was murdered, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to Pingliang; Zhangsun Jian took part in every major plan and policy.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，留儉為秦州長史。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Houmochen Yue, [Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai] left Jian as Chief Clerk of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was defeated, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai left Zhangsun Jian behind as chief clerk of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 時西夏州仍未內屬，而東魏遣許和為刺史，儉以信義招之，和乃舉州歸附。

translations.literal: At the time Western Xia Province still had not submitted internally, yet Eastern Wei sent Xu He as governor; Jian with faith and righteousness won him over, and He then raised the whole province in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia Province had not yet submitted, but Eastern Wei had sent Xu He as its governor; Zhangsun Jian won him over with good faith, and Xu He brought the whole province over.

sentences.zh: 卽以儉為西夏州刺史，總統三夏州。

translations.literal: [Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai] immediately made Jian Governor of Western Xia Province, with overall command of the three Xia provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then made Zhangsun Jian governor of Western Xia Province with overall authority over the three Xia provinces.

sentences.zh: 時荊襄初附，太祖表儉功績尤美，宜委東南之任，授荊州刺史、東南道行臺僕射。

translations.literal: At the time Jing and Xiang had newly submitted; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai memorialized that Jian's achievements were especially excellent and he should be entrusted with the southeastern appointment, granting him Governor of Jing Province and Vice Director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang had just submitted, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai memorialized that Zhangsun Jian's record was outstanding and that the southeast should be entrusted to him; he was made governor of Jing Province and vice director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Office.

sentences.zh: 所部鄭縣令泉璨為民所訟，推治獲實。

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Zheng County in his jurisdiction, Quan Can, was sued by the people; investigation established the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Can, magistrate of Zheng County in his jurisdiction, was denounced by the people, and an inquiry proved the charges true.

sentences.zh: 儉卽大集僚屬而謂之曰：「此由刺史教誨不明，信不被物，是我之愆，非泉璨之罪。

translations.literal: Jian then greatly gathered his staff and said to them: "This is because the governor's instruction and guidance were not clear, and trust did not reach the people—it is my fault, not Quan Can's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian then assembled his entire staff and said: "This happened because I failed to teach and lead clearly enough for trust to reach the people. The fault is mine, not Quan Can's.

sentences.zh: 」遂於廳事前，肉袒自罰，舍璨不問。

translations.literal: " Thereupon before the hall gate he bared his torso and punished himself, and released Can from inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He then bared his back in the courtyard before the hall, flogged himself, and dismissed the case against Quan Can.

sentences.zh: 於是屬城肅勵，莫敢犯法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the subordinate cities became solemnly disciplined, and none dared violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the subordinate districts stood in awe, and no one dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝璽書勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei sent a sealed letter commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei sent him an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 太祖又與儉書曰：「近行路傳公以部內縣令有罪，遂自杖三十，用肅羣下。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also wrote to Jian saying: "Recently travelers report that because a county magistrate within your department had guilt, you then self-cane thirty strokes to solemnize the subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also wrote to Zhangsun Jian: "Travelers lately tell me that when a county magistrate under you was found guilty, you had yourself beaten thirty strokes to awe your staff.

sentences.zh: 吾昔聞『王臣謇謇，匪躬之故』，蓋謂憂公忘私，知無不為而已。

translations.literal: I formerly heard "king's ministers are forthright, for the sake of not the person alone"—this broadly means worrying for the public and forgetting the private, knowing nothing and not acting—but [only] this.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the saying that a king's minister must speak plainly and forget himself for the realm's sake—that is, to care for the public good and hold nothing back. Yet that is only the common measure.

sentences.zh: 未有如公刻身罰己以訓羣僚者也。

translations.literal: Never has there been like you, carving the body to punish the self to instruct the many officials.
translations.idiomatic: Never have I known a man who punished his own body to teach his colleagues, as you have done.

sentences.zh: 聞之嘉歎。

translations.literal: Hearing this I rejoice and sigh [in admiration]."
translations.idiomatic: When I heard of it, I marveled and rejoiced."

sentences.zh: 」荊蠻舊俗，少不敬長。

translations.literal: The old custom of the Jing barbarians: the young did not respect their elders.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jing tribes the old custom held that the young owed little respect to their elders.

sentences.zh: 儉殷勤勸導，風俗大革。

translations.literal: Jian diligently counseled and guided, and customs greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian worked patiently to guide them, and local customs changed profoundly.

sentences.zh: 務廣耕桑，兼習武事，故得邊境無虞，民安其業。

translations.literal: He devoted effort to expanding agriculture and sericulture, while also practicing military affairs; thus the border had no worry, and the people were secure in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed farming and mulberry cultivation while keeping the people trained for war, so the frontier stayed quiet and the people could live by their trades in peace.

sentences.zh: 吏民表請為儉構清德樓，樹碑刻頌，朝議許焉。

translations.literal: Officials and people submitted a petition to build Pure Virtue Tower for Jian, erect a stele and inscribe praise; court deliberation granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners petitioned to build a Pure Virtue Tower for Zhangsun Jian and to raise a stele in his praise; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 在州遂歷

translations.literal: In the province he then served for
translations.idiomatic: He served in the province for

translations.literal: (two)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: two]

sentences.zh: ［七］載。

translations.literal: [seven] years.
translations.idiomatic: seven years.

sentences.zh: 徵授大行臺尚書，兼相府司馬。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Grand Executive Office Minister, concurrently Grand Chancellor's Office Major.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed minister of the Grand Executive Office, while also serving as major of the grand chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 嘗與羣公侍坐于太祖，及退，太祖謂左右曰：「此公閒雅，孤每與語，嘗肅然畏敬，恐有所失。

translations.literal: Once with the various lords he attended seated before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; when they withdrew, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to those at his side: "This lord is leisurely and elegant; every time I speak with him, I am always solemnly awed and respectful, fearing I may fail in something.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while sitting with the other lords in attendance on Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, he withdrew with them afterward; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told his attendants: "That man is refined and easy in manner. Whenever I talk with him I find myself sitting up straight in awe, afraid I may say something unworthy.

sentences.zh: 」他日，太祖謂儉曰：「名實理須相稱，尚書旣志安貧素，可改名儉，以彰雅操。」

translations.literal: " Another day, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Jian: "Name and reality by principle must match each other; the Minister since his ambition is to settle in poverty and simplicity, may change his name to Jian, to display elegant conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Another day Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Zhangsun Jian: "Name and conduct ought to match. You, Minister, aspire to live plainly and without excess; you should take the name Jian to show that refinement."

sentences.zh: 又除行臺僕射、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Again removed [from current post] and made Executive Office Vice Director and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed vice director of the executive office and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時梁岳陽王蕭詧內附，初遣使入朝，至荊州。

translations.literal: At the time Liang's Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha internally submitted, first sent envoys to court, arriving at Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liang Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, had submitted to the court and sent his first embassy through Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 儉於廳事列軍儀，具戎服，與使人以賓主禮相見。

translations.literal: Jian in the hall arranged military ceremony, fully equipped martial garb, and with the envoys met using host-and-guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the reception hall Zhangsun Jian drew up a military guard, put on full martial dress, and received the envoys with formal host-and-guest ceremony.

sentences.zh: 儉容貌魁偉，音聲如鐘，大為鮮卑語，遣人傳譯以問客。

translations.literal: Jian's appearance was imposing and grand, his voice like a bell; he spoke much in Xianbei language, and sent men to translate and interpret to question the guests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian was towering in build and spoke in a deep, bell-like voice; he addressed them at length in Xianbei and had interpreters relay his questions.

sentences.zh: 客惶恐不敢仰視。

translations.literal: The guests in fear and trepidation did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were so awed that they did not dare raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 日晚，儉乃著裙襦紗帽，引客宴於別齋。

translations.literal: When evening came, Jian then wore skirt-robe and gauze cap, and led the guests to feast in a separate study.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he changed into civilian skirt-robe and gauze cap and entertained the guests at a separate banquet.

sentences.zh: 因序梁國喪亂，朝廷招攜之意，發言可觀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he narrated the Liang state's calamity and chaos, and the court's intent to receive and embrace; his words were worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke of the Liang realm's ruin and of the court's wish to welcome and restore them; his remarks were eloquent and compelling.

sentences.zh: 使人大悅。

translations.literal: The envoys greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 出曰：「吾所不能測也。」

translations.literal: On leaving they said: "What we could not fathom."
translations.idiomatic: When they departed they said, "He is beyond our power to measure."

sentences.zh: 及梁元帝嗣位於江陵，外敦鄰睦，內懷異計。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Yuan succeeded to the throne at Jiangling, externally he was sincere in neighborly harmony, internally he harbored a different plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiangling, he cultivated neighborly courtesy abroad while secretly nursing other designs.

sentences.zh: 儉密啟太祖，陳攻取之謀。

translations.literal: Jian secretly reported to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, stating a plan to attack and take [Jiangling].
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian secretly reported to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and laid out a plan to seize Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 於是徵儉入朝，問其經略。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jian was summoned to court to be asked his grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then summoned Zhangsun Jian to court and asked for his strategy.

sentences.zh: 儉對曰：「今江陵旣在江北，去我不遠。

translations.literal: Jian replied: "Now Jiangling is already north of the Yangtze, not far from us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian answered: "Jiangling now lies north of the Yangtze, close at hand.

sentences.zh: 湘東卽位，已涉三年。

translations.literal: Xiangdong succeeded to the throne, already spanning three years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Xiangdong has already reigned three years.

sentences.zh: 觀其形勢，不欲東下。

translations.literal: Observing its situation and power, it does not wish to move east.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the situation, he has no wish to march east.

sentences.zh: 骨肉相殘，民厭其毒。

translations.literal: Flesh and bone mutually slaughter; the people are weary of its poison.
translations.idiomatic: His own kin have torn one another apart, and the people are sick of the suffering.

sentences.zh: 荊州軍資器械，儲積已久，若大軍西討，必無匱乏之慮。

translations.literal: Jing Province's military stores and weapons have been accumulated long; if a great army westward punishes, there will surely be no fear of shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province has long hoarded arms and supplies; if a great army moves west, we need not fear want.

sentences.zh: 且兼弱攻昧，武之善經。

translations.literal: Moreover "combining against the weak and attacking the dim"—this is warfare's excellent constant.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, to join against the weak and strike the blind is the finest rule of war.

sentences.zh: 國家旣有蜀土，若更平江漢，撫而安之，收其貢賦，以供軍國，天下不足定也。

translations.literal: The state already has Shu territory; if further pacifying Jiang-Han, comforting and settling it, collecting its tribute and levies to supply army and state, all under Heaven would not be difficult to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The realm already holds Shu; if we also pacify the Jiang-Han region, soothe and settle it, and take its tribute and taxes for army and state, the rest of the empire will not be hard to secure.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深然之，乃謂儉曰：「如公之言，吾取之晚矣。

translations.literal: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai deeply agreed, then said to Jian: "As you say, I have taken it too late.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai strongly agreed and said to Zhangsun Jian: "As you say, I have moved too late.

sentences.zh: 」令儉還州，密為之備。

translations.literal: " He ordered Jian to return to the province and secretly prepare.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhangsun Jian back to his province to make secret preparations."

sentences.zh: 尋令柱國、燕公于謹總戎衆伐江陵。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered Pillar of State, Duke of Yan Yu Jin to command the army masses to attack Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he put Pillar of State Yu Jin, Duke of Yan, in command of the army for the assault on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 平，以儉元謀，賞奴婢三百口。

translations.literal: When pacified, because Jian was the original planner, rewarded with three hundred male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Zhangsun Jian was rewarded with three hundred slaves as the original architect of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太祖與儉書曰：「本圖江陵，由公畫計，今果如所言。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wrote to Jian: "Originally planning Jiangling, it was by your drawing up the plan—now it indeed is as you spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wrote to Zhangsun Jian: "The plan for Jiangling was yours from the start, and events have proved you right.

sentences.zh: 智者見未萌，何其妙也。

translations.literal: The wise see before sprouting—how wondrous.
translations.idiomatic: The wise foresee what has not yet budded—how subtle your insight was.

sentences.zh: 但吳民離散，事藉招懷，南服重鎮，非公莫可。

translations.literal: But Wu people's are scattered and dispersed; the affair relies on receiving and embracing; the southern domain's important fortress—none but you can [hold it]."
translations.idiomatic: But the people of Wu are scattered and must be won back by kindness; no one but you can hold this great southern stronghold."

sentences.zh: 」遂令儉鎮江陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Jian to garrison Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Zhangsun Jian in charge of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 進爵昌寧公，遷大將軍，移鎮荊州，總管五十二州。

translations.literal: Advanced in rank to Duke of Changning, transferred to Grand General, moved garrison to Jing Province, overall administering fifty-two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian was raised to Duke of Changning and grand general, moved his headquarters to Jing Province, and took overall command of fifty-two provinces.

sentences.zh: 儉舊嘗詣闕奏事，時值大雪，遂立於雪中待報，自旦達暮，竟無惰容。

translations.literal: Jian formerly once went to the palace gate to report affairs; at the time there fell great snow; he then stood in the snow awaiting reply, from dawn reaching dusk—throughout no lazy expression.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Zhangsun Jian went to the palace to report on affairs, a heavy snow was falling; he stood in the snow from morning until night waiting for an answer, never once showing weariness.

sentences.zh: 其奉公勤至，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His serving the public with diligence and utmost effort—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His devotion to duty was always of this order.

sentences.zh: 三年，以疾還京。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of illness returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 為夏州總管，薨，遺啟世宗，請葬于太祖陵側，並以官所賜之宅還官。

translations.literal: Served as Overall Commander of Xia Province; died; left memorial to Emperor Shizong requesting burial beside Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's tomb, and also returning to the state the residence granted by office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall commander of Xia Province, then died; in his final memorial to Emperor Shizong he asked to be buried beside Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's tomb and to return to the state the house he had received as an official grant.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: Edicts all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted both requests.

sentences.zh: 追封鄶公。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Kuai.

sentences.zh: 荊民儀同趙超等七百人，感儉遺愛，詣闕請為儉立廟樹碑，詔許之。

translations.literal: Jing people Honorary Companion Zhao Chao and others, seven hundred men, moved by Jian's legacy of love, went to the palace gate requesting to establish a temple and erect stele for Jian; edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred men of Jing, led by honorary companion Zhao Chao, moved by Zhangsun Jian's lingering kindness, petitioned at court to build him a temple and stele; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔叔敖辭沃壤之地，蕭何就窮僻之鄉，以古方今，無慚曩哲。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Formerly Shu Ao declined fertile lands, Xiao He took a poor and remote village—comparing ancient with present, one need not be shamed before past sages.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Long ago Shu Ao refused rich land and Xiao He settled in a poor, remote place; measured against those ancients, Zhangsun Jian need not blush before the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 言尋嘉尚，弗忘于懷。

translations.literal: Speaking of seeking worthy admiration, not forgetting in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Such virtue deserves lasting remembrance.

sentences.zh: 而有司未達大體，遽以其第卽便給外。

translations.literal: Yet the officials did not grasp the grand principle and hastily with his mansion immediately gave it to outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the officials failed to understand the larger meaning and had hastily turned his house over to others.

sentences.zh: 今還其妻子。

translations.literal: Now return his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Let his wife and children have it back.

sentences.zh: 」子隆。

translations.literal: " His son Long.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Long.

sentences.zh: 長孫紹遠字師，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Shaoyuan, styled Shi, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shaoyuan, styled Shi, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少名仁。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Ren.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was called Ren.

sentences.zh: 父稚，魏太師、錄尚書、上黨王。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Wei Grand Preceptor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been Grand Preceptor of Wei, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 紹遠性寬容，有大度，望之儼然，朋儕莫敢褻狎。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan by nature was broad and tolerant, had great magnanimity; viewed he was solemnly composed, and companions did not dare treat him with familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shaoyuan was open-hearted and magnanimous; he looked so grave and dignified that even his peers dared not treat him lightly.

sentences.zh: 雅好墳籍，聰慧過人。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved tomb records [classics], his intelligence surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics and was unusually quick of mind.

sentences.zh: 時稚作牧壽春，紹遠幼，年甫十三。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi served as governor of Shouchun; Shaoyuan was young, his years just thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his father Zhi was governor of Shouchun; Zhangsun Shaoyuan was only thirteen.

sentences.zh: 稚管記王碩聞紹遠強記，心以為不然。

translations.literal: Zhi's registrar Wang Shuo heard of Shaoyuan's powerful memory and in his heart thought it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's registrar Wang Shuo heard that Zhangsun Shaoyuan had a prodigious memory and did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 遂白稚曰：「伏承世子聰慧之姿，發於天性，目所一見，誦之於口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reported to Zhi saying: "I humbly learn the heir's brilliant talent, arising from innate nature—what the eyes see once, the mouth recites.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told Zhi: "I hear that the heir's brilliance is inborn—that what he sees once he can recite at once.

sentences.zh: 此旣曆世罕有，竊願驗之。

translations.literal: This is already rare through the ages; I privately wish to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Such a gift is all but unheard of in any age, and I would like to put it to the test.

sentences.zh: 」於是命紹遠試焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Shaoyuan to be tested.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then had Zhangsun Shaoyuan tested."

sentences.zh: 讀《月令》數紙，纔一遍，誦之若流。

translations.literal: Reading several pages of the Monthly Ordinance, just one time through, he recited it like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: He read several pages of the Monthly Ordinances once through and recited them fluently from memory.

sentences.zh: 自是碩乃歎服。

translations.literal: From this Shuo then sighed in admiration and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Wang Shuo was fully convinced.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，累遷司徒右長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei he rose to chief clerk of the right under the Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武稱兵而帝西遷，紹遠隨稚奔赴。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops and the Emperor migrated west, Shaoyuan followed Zhi in hurrying to join.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan took up arms and the emperor moved west, Zhangsun Shaoyuan went with his father to join him.

sentences.zh: 又累遷殿中尚書、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Again repeatedly promoted to Palace Master of Writing and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to palace master of writing and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太祖每謂羣公曰：「長孫公任使之處，令人無反顧憂。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often said to the various lords: "Where Lord Zhangsun is assigned and employed, it makes people have no worry of looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often told the other ministers: "Wherever Lord Zhangsun is placed in office, men serve without looking back over their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 漢之蕭、寇，何足多也。

translations.literal: Han's Xiao and Kou—how could they be counted as much.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao and Kou of Han were nothing beside him.

sentences.zh: 然其容止堂堂，足為當今模楷。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing and deportment are dignified and imposing, sufficient to serve as today's model.
translations.idiomatic: And his bearing is so upright and commanding that he is a model for our own age.

sentences.zh: 」六官建，拜大司樂。

translations.literal: " When the Six Offices were established, appointed Grand Master of Music.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, Zhangsun Shaoyuan was made grand master of music."

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，封上黨公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 初，紹遠為太常，廣召工人，創造樂器，土木絲竹，各得其宜。

translations.literal: Initially, Shaoyuan as Grand Master of Ceremonial broadly summoned craftsmen, created musical instruments; wood, clay, silk, and bamboo—each obtained its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as grand master of ceremonial, Zhangsun Shaoyuan gathered craftsmen from far and wide to make new instruments, fitting wood, clay, silk, and bamboo each to its proper use.

sentences.zh: 為黃鐘不調，紹遠每以為意。

translations.literal: Because the yellow bell was not in tune, Shaoyuan always took it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow bell pitch would not settle, and the problem weighed on him constantly.

sentences.zh: 嘗因退朝，經韓使君佛寺前過，浮圖三層之上，有鳴鐸焉。

translations.literal: Once upon returning from court, passing before Han Shijun's Buddhist temple, atop the three-story pagoda there was a sounding bell-clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Once, leaving court, he passed Han Shijun's Buddhist temple and noticed a sounding bell on the three-tiered pagoda.

sentences.zh: 忽聞其音，雅合宮調，取而配奏，方始克諧。

translations.literal: Suddenly hearing its sound, it elegantly matched the gong mode; taking it to pair and play, only then achieved harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard it strike, the tone matched the gong pitch perfectly; he took the bell, matched it in performance, and at last achieved harmony.

sentences.zh: 紹遠乃啟世宗行之。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan thereupon reported to Emperor Shizong to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shaoyuan then memorialized Emperor Shizong to adopt it.

sentences.zh: 紹遠所奏樂，以八為數。

translations.literal: The music Shaoyuan presented used eight as the number.
translations.idiomatic: The music Zhangsun Shaoyuan submitted took eight as its governing number.

sentences.zh: 故梁黃門侍郎裴正上書，以為昔者大舜欲聞七始，下洎周武，爰創七音。

translations.literal: Former Liang Attendant Secretary of the Yellow Gate Pei Zheng submitted a memorial, holding that in antiquity Great Shun wished to hear the Seven Beginnings, and down through King Wu of Zhou thereupon created the seven tones.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, former Attendant Secretary of the Yellow Gate of Liang, submitted a memorial arguing that in antiquity Great Shun had wished to hear the Seven Beginnings and that, down to King Wu of Zhou, the seven tones were first established.

sentences.zh: 持林鐘作黃鐘，以為正調之首。

translations.literal: He took Forest Bell as Yellow Bell to serve as the head of the correct tuning.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Forest Bell as Yellow Bell and made it the head of the standard pitch sequence.

sentences.zh: 詔與紹遠詳議往復，於是遂定以八為數焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered detailed discussion back and forth with Shaoyuan; thereupon it was fixed to take eight as the number.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhangsun Shaoyuan to debate the matter in detail; the court then fixed the number at eight.

sentences.zh: 授小司空。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lesser Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng was appointed Lesser Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖讀史書，見武王克殷而作七始，又欲廢八而懸七，幷除黃鐘之正宮，用林鐘為調首。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu read the historical records and, seeing that King Wu, on conquering Yin, created the Seven Beginnings, again wished to abolish eight and suspend seven, also removing Yellow Bell as the correct palace tone and using Forest Bell as the head of the tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu read the histories and, seeing that King Wu had created the Seven Beginnings after conquering Yin, again wished to abolish the eight-tone system and suspend seven sets, remove Yellow Bell as the principal palace pitch, and use Forest Bell as the leading tone.

sentences.zh: 紹遠奏云：「天子懸八，肇自先民，百王共軌，萬世不易。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan memorialized, saying: "The Son of Heaven suspends eight—this began with the ancients; a hundred kings shared one standard, unchanging for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shaoyuan memorialized: "The Son of Heaven suspends eight sets of bells and chimes—a practice reaching back to antiquity, shared by a hundred kings and unchanging through the ages.

sentences.zh: 下逮周武，甫修七始之音。

translations.literal: Down to King Wu of Zhou, he only repaired the tones of the Seven Beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Down to King Wu of Zhou, he merely restored the music of the Seven Beginnings.

sentences.zh: 詳諸經義，又無廢八之典。

translations.literal: Examining all the canonical teachings, there is again no precedent for abolishing eight.
translations.idiomatic: A careful reading of the canonical texts offers no precedent for abolishing the eight-tone system.

sentences.zh: 且黃鐘為君，天子正位，今欲廢之，未見其可。

translations.literal: Moreover Yellow Bell is the ruler; it is the Son of Heaven's correct position—now to wish to abolish it, one does not see how this could be right.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yellow Bell is the sovereign pitch and the Son of Heaven's proper station; to abolish it now seems impossible to justify.

sentences.zh: 」後高祖竟

translations.literal: " Later Emperor Gaozu in the end
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Emperor Gaozu

translations.literal: (abolished)
translations.idiomatic: (abolished) [deleted character]

sentences.zh: 〔行〕七音。

translations.literal: [implemented] the seven tones.
translations.idiomatic: implemented the seven-tone system.

sentences.zh: 屬紹遠遘疾，未獲面陳，慮有司遽損樂器，乃書與樂部齊樹之。

translations.literal: Just then Shaoyuan fell ill; unable to state his views in person, fearing the relevant offices would hastily reduce the musical instruments, he wrote to Qi Shuzhi of the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhangsun Shaoyuan fell ill. Unable to present his views in person and fearing that the relevant offices would hastily cut back the instruments, he wrote to Qi Shuzhi of the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 澄字士亮。

translations.literal: Cheng, styled Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, styled Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，司徒李琰之見而奇之，遂以女妻焉。

translations.literal: At age ten, Minister over the Masses Li Yanzhi saw him and was struck by him; he thereupon gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he so impressed Minister over the Masses Li Yanzhi that Li gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 十四，從征討，有策謀，勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: At fourteen, he followed on campaigns; he had strategy and counsel, and his bravery ranked above all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he joined campaigns, showed strategic talent, and outstripped the other generals in courage.

sentences.zh: 及長，容貌魁岸，風儀溫雅。

translations.literal: When grown, his appearance was imposing and his bearing warm and refined.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was tall and imposing, with a warm and refined bearing.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，除征東將軍、渭州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was appointed General Pacifying the East and Governor of Wei Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he was made General Pacifying the East and Governor of Wei Province.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嘗與太祖及羣公宴，從容言曰：「《孝經》一卷，人行之本，諸公宜各引要言。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once feasted with Grand Progenitor and the assembled lords and said at ease: "The Classic of Filial Piety in one scroll is the root of human conduct—gentlemen should each quote a key saying.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once feasted with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and the assembled lords and said at ease: "The Classic of Filial Piety in one scroll is the root of human conduct. Gentlemen, each of you should quote a key passage.

sentences.zh: 」澄應聲曰：「夙夜匪懈，以事一人。

translations.literal: " Cheng responded promptly: "Be untiring from morning to night in serving one man."
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng answered at once: "Be untiring from morning to night in serving one man."

sentences.zh: 」座中有人次曰：「匡救其惡。

translations.literal: " Someone seated there next said: "Rescue him from his evil."
translations.idiomatic: " Someone else at the table said: "Rescue him from his evil."

sentences.zh: 」旣而出閤，太祖深歎澄之合機，而譴其次答者。

translations.literal: " When they left the pavilion, Grand Progenitor deeply praised Cheng for hitting the mark, and rebuked the one who answered next.
translations.idiomatic: " After they left the pavilion, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai greatly praised Cheng for hitting the mark and rebuked the man who had answered next.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖援玉壁，又從戰邙山，進位驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Later he followed Grand Progenitor in relieving Yubi and again fought at Mount Mang; he was advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to relieve Yubi and fought again at Mount Mang; he was raised to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，拜大將軍，封義門公，為玉壁總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Yimen, and made overall commander of Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, he was made Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Yimen, and appointed overall commander of Yubi.

sentences.zh: 卒，自喪初至及葬，世宗三臨之。

translations.literal: When he died, from the start of mourning to the burial, Emperor Ming visited three times.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, from the start of mourning through the burial, Emperor Ming visited three times.

sentences.zh: 典祀中大夫宇文容諫曰：「君臨臣喪，自有節制。

translations.literal: Palace Sacrifice Grand Master Yuwen Rong remonstrated, saying: "A lord visiting a minister's mourning has its own limits.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Sacrifice Grand Master Yuwen Rong remonstrated: "When a sovereign attends a minister's mourning, ritual sets clear limits.

sentences.zh: 今乘輿屢降，恐乖禮典。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage has repeatedly descended—this may violate ritual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For the imperial carriage to descend so often may violate ritual precedent.

sentences.zh: 」世宗不從。

translations.literal: " Emperor Ming did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Ming did not listen.

sentences.zh: 澄操履清約，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Cheng's conduct was pure and frugal; his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng lived plainly and frugally; his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂曰：「我於公間，志無所惜，公有所須，宜卽具道。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor once said to him: "Between us I hold back nothing in my heart—whatever you need, you should state it at once."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told him: "Between us I hold back nothing. If you need anything, say so at once."

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「澄自頂至足，皆是明公恩造。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "From crown to sole, Cheng is entirely the product of your grace.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng said: "From head to foot I owe everything to your grace.

sentences.zh: 卽如今者，實無所須。

translations.literal: Even as things are now, I truly need nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Even now I truly need nothing.

sentences.zh: 」雅對賓客，接引忘疲。

translations.literal: " He gracefully received guests, attending them without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: " He received guests with grace and attended them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 雖不飲酒，而好觀人酣興。

translations.literal: Though he did not drink, he loved watching others in the flush of intoxication.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not drink himself, he loved watching others in the flush of wine.

sentences.zh: 常恐座客請歸，每勅中廚別進異饌，留之止。

translations.literal: He often feared guests at table would ask to leave; he always ordered the central kitchen to bring special fare separately to keep them and make them stay.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing guests would ask to leave, he always had the central kitchen send out special dishes to keep them at table.

sentences.zh: 兕字若汗，性機辯，強記博聞，雅重賓游，尤善談論。

translations.literal: Si, styled Ruohan, was by nature quick and eloquent, with a strong memory and wide learning; he greatly valued guests and fellowship and was especially skilled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Si, styled Ruohan, was quick and eloquent by nature, with a strong memory and wide learning; he greatly valued guests and fellowship and was especially skilled at conversation.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the westward migration.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the westward migration.

sentences.zh: 天和初，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府，遷絳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, after successive promotions he became Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office, then was transferred as Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhe, after successive promotions he became Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office, then was transferred as Governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 斛斯徵字士亮，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Sizheng, styled Shiliang, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng, styled Shiliang, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父椿，太傅、尚書令。

translations.literal: His father Chun was Grand Tutor and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun was Grand Tutor and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 徵幼聰穎，五歲誦《孝經》、《周易》，識者異之。

translations.literal: Sizheng from youth was clever and keen; at five he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety and Book of Changes—those who knew him were struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hu Sizheng was clever and keen; at five he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety and the Book of Changes, and those who knew him marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉羣書，尤精《三禮》，兼解音律。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged widely through books, especially mastering the Three Ritual Classics, and also understood pitch and rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he read widely, mastered the Three Ritual Classics above all, and also understood pitch and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 有至性，居父喪，朝夕共一溢米。

translations.literal: He had utmost filial nature: mourning his father, morning and evening he ate together only one yi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, in mourning his father he ate only one yi of rice morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 以父勳累遷太常卿。

translations.literal: By his father's merit he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: By his father's merit he rose repeatedly to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自魏孝武西遷，雅樂廢缺，徵博采遺逸，稽諸典故，創新改舊，方始備焉。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's westward migration, court music had been lost and broken; Sizheng broadly gathered what survived, examined canonical precedent, created anew and reformed the old—and only then was it complete.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's westward migration court music had fallen into ruin; Hu Sizheng gathered what survived, checked it against canonical precedent, and by creating anew and reforming the old at last restored it.

sentences.zh: 又樂有錞于者，近代絕無此器，或有自蜀得之，皆莫之識。

translations.literal: Moreover in music there is the chunyu—in recent times this instrument had completely ceased to exist; when some obtained one from Shu, none recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: Music also includes the chunyu, an instrument long extinct in recent times; when one was brought from Shu, no one recognized it.

sentences.zh: 徵見之曰：「此錞于也。

translations.literal: Sizheng saw it and said: "This is a chunyu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng saw it and said: "This is a chunyu.

sentences.zh: 」衆弗之信。

translations.literal: " The crowd did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: " No one believed him.

sentences.zh: 徵遂依干寶《周禮注》以芒筒捋之，其聲極振，衆乃歎服。

translations.literal: Sizheng thereupon, following Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou, used a bamboo tube to strike it; the sound was extremely resonant, and the crowd then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng then followed Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou and struck it with a bamboo tube; the sound rang out powerfully, and the onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 徵乃取以合樂焉。

translations.literal: Sizheng then took it to combine with the music.
translations.idiomatic: He then incorporated it into the court music.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜司樂中大夫，進位驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Master Director of Music, and advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was made Grand Master Director of Music and advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 後高祖以徵治經有師法，詔令教授皇太子。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu, because Sizheng's handling of the classics had received-method orthodoxy, issued an edict ordering him to instruct the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Gaozu, finding Hu Sizheng's teaching of the classics authoritative, ordered him to instruct the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時為魯公，與諸皇子等咸服青衿，行束修之禮，受業於徵，仍並呼徵為夫子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Duke of Lu, he and the other princes all wore the blue collar, performed the ceremony of bundled dried meat, received instruction from Sizheng, and all called Sizheng "Master."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was Duke of Lu, he and the other princes all wore the scholar's blue collar, performed the ceremony of bundled dried meat, studied under Hu Sizheng, and all called him Master.

sentences.zh: 儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，遷上大將軍、大宗伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Upper Grand General and Grand Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Hu Sizheng was transferred to Upper Grand General and Grand Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時高祖初崩，梓宮在殯，帝意欲速葬，令朝臣議之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just died and the coffin was still in temporary burial; the emperor wished a speedy burial and ordered the court ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just died and the coffin was still in temporary burial; the emperor wished to bury him quickly and ordered the court to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 徵與內史宇文孝伯等固請依禮七月，帝竟不許。

translations.literal: Sizheng and Inner Scribe Yuwen Xiaobo and others firmly requested observing the seven-month rite, but the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng, Inner Scribe Yuwen Xiaobo, and others firmly asked that the seven-month mourning rite be observed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 帝之為太子也，宮尹鄭譯坐不能以正道調護，被謫除名。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been crown prince, Palace Superintendent Zheng Yi had been demoted and removed from office for failing to guide and protect him by the correct way.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been crown prince, Palace Superintendent Zheng Yi had been demoted and dismissed for failing to guide him properly.

sentences.zh: 而帝雅親愛譯，至是拜譯內史中大夫，甚委任之。

translations.literal: But the emperor had long been fond of Yi; at this point he appointed Yi Inner Scribe Senior Grand Master and entrusted him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor had long been fond of Zheng Yi; he now made him Inner Scribe Senior Grand Master and entrusted him heavily.

sentences.zh: 譯乃獻新樂，十二月各一笙，每一笙用十六管。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon presented new music: each month had one sheng, and each sheng used sixteen pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi thereupon presented new music: one sheng for each month, each sheng using sixteen pipes.

sentences.zh: 帝令與徵議之，徵駁而奏，帝頗納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered deliberation with Sizheng; Sizheng rebutted and submitted a memorial, and the emperor largely accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hu Sizheng to discuss it with him; Sizheng rebutted the proposal in a memorial, and the emperor largely accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 及高祖山陵還，帝欲作樂，復令議其可不。

translations.literal: When the procession returned from Emperor Gaozu's mount tomb, the emperor wished to perform music and again ordered discussion of whether it was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession returned from Emperor Gaozu's tomb, the emperor wished to perform music and again ordered the court to debate whether it was permissible.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「《孝經》云『聞樂不樂』。

translations.literal: Sizheng said: "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music, one is not joyful.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng said: "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music, one is not joyful.'"

sentences.zh: 聞尚不樂，其況作乎。

translations.literal: If even hearing music brings no joy, how much more making it?
translations.idiomatic: If even hearing music brings no joy, how much less should one perform it?

sentences.zh: 」鄭譯曰：「旣云聞樂，明卽非無。

translations.literal: " Zheng Yi said: "Since it says 'hearing music,' that clearly means music is not absent.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Yi said: "Since the text says 'hearing music,' music clearly exists.

sentences.zh: 止可不樂，何容不奏。

translations.literal: Only one need not be joyful—how can one fail to perform it?
translations.idiomatic: One need only refrain from joy—how can one refuse to perform it altogether?

sentences.zh: 」帝遂依譯議。

translations.literal: " The emperor then followed Yi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then followed Zheng Yi's view.

sentences.zh: 譯因此銜之。

translations.literal: Yi thereby harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi thereby nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 帝后肆行非度，昏虐日甚。

translations.literal: After this the emperor wantonly overstepped measure; his delusion and cruelty grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor wantonly overstepped all bounds, and his folly and cruelty grew daily.

sentences.zh: 徵以荷高祖重恩，嘗備位師傅，若生不能諫，死何以見高祖。

translations.literal: Sizheng, bearing the heavy grace of Emperor Gaozu and having once held the post of tutor, thought: if in life he could not remonstrate, how in death could he face Emperor Gaozu?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng, deeply indebted to Emperor Gaozu and having once served as tutor, thought: if he could not remonstrate while alive, how could he face Emperor Gaozu after death?

sentences.zh: 乃上疏極諫，指陳帝失，帝不納。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance, pointing out the emperor's faults; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, listing the emperor's faults; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 譯因譖之，遂下徵獄。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon slandered him, and Sizheng was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi thereupon slandered him, and Hu Sizheng was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 獄卒張元哀之，乃以佩刀穿獄牆，遂出之。

translations.literal: The jailer Zhang Yuan pitied him; using his girdle knife he pierced the prison wall and thus got him out.
translations.idiomatic: The jailer Zhang Yuan took pity on him, used his girdle knife to break through the prison wall, and got him out.

sentences.zh: 元卒被拷而終無所言。

translations.literal: Yuan was beaten in interrogation but to the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan was tortured in interrogation but never spoke.

sentences.zh: 徵遇赦得免。

translations.literal: Sizheng met an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng was spared when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 隋文踐極，例復官，除太子太傅，詔修撰樂書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, by precedent his office was restored; he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and ordered to compile a book on music.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Hu Sizheng was restored to office by precedent, made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, and ordered to compile a book on music.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，薨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he died.

sentences.zh: 子諺。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yan.

sentences.zh: 徵所撰《樂典》十卷。

translations.literal: Sizheng compiled the Music Canon in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizheng compiled the Music Canon in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
